title: To build an AI-powered retail intelligence platform that delivers real-time shopper analytics, automated inventory visibility, and proactive queue management through on-device AI,enabling retailers to reduce stock-outs, improve customer experience, optimize staffing, and increase operational efficiency while maintaining privacy and minimizing cloud dependency.
description:
Background India's retail sector includes millions of neighborhood stores, supermarkets,pharmacies, and large-format retail outlets that serve high customer volumes every day. Retailers face challenges such as inventory shrinkage, stock-outs, long billing queues, inefficient shelf replenishment, and limited visibility into shopper behavior. Many stores, especially in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities, also operate with constrained internet connectivity and require solutions that can function reliably without continuous cloud access.
Recent advances in edge AI allow cameras and sensors to perform real-time analytics directly on local devices, enabling faster decisions, improved privacy,reduced bandwidth consumption, and uninterrupted operation even during connectivity outages. Hybrid and edge AI approaches are increasingly being adopted for real-time monitoring and decision support across multiple industries.
Description Design an Intelligent Retail Analytics System that uses smart cameras and on-device AI to monitor retail operations in real time. The system should analyze shopper movement, inventory levels, and checkout queues without requiring constant cloud processing.The solution should automatically identify customer traffic patterns, measure dwell time in different store sections, detect out-of-stock products, monitor shelf compliance, and predict queue congestion before it impacts customer experience.AI inference should happen locally on the edge devices to enable low-latency decisions while preserving customer privacy and minimizing network dependency.The system should convert video streams into actionable business insights that help retailers improve operational efficiency, optimize staffing, increase product availability, and enhance customer satisfaction. Edge-based analytics can provide real-time intelligence while reducing dependence on cloud connectivity.
Expected Solution The proposed solution should implement some or all of the following:
1. Shopper Analytics
• Detect and count customers entering and exiting the store.
• Analyze footfall trends by time, day, and store zone.
• Measure shopper dwell time near products and promotional displays.
• Generate heatmaps showing customer movement patterns.
2. Inventory Monitoring
• Detect low-stock and out-of-stock situations using shelf-facing cameras.
• Monitor planogram compliance and product placement.
• Alert store staff when replenishment is required.
• Track merchandise availability in real time.
3. Queue Intelligence
• Monitor checkout counters and queue lengths.
• Predict congestion before queues become excessive.
• Recommend opening additional billing counters.
• Measure average waiting and service times.
4. Edge AI Processing
• Run all computer vision models locally on edge hardware.
• Operate even during internet disruptions.
• Reduce cloud bandwidth and operational costs.
• Support rapid, low-latency decision-making.
5. Privacy-Aware Analytics
• Use anonymous people detection and tracking.
• Avoid storing personally identifiable information.
• Process sensitive data locally where possible.
6. Store Operations Dashboard
• Real-time alerts for stock shortages and queue build-up.
• Daily and weekly analytics reports.
• KPI visualization including footfall, conversion indicators, inventory status, and staff efficiency.
7. Scalable Deployment
• Support deployment across small stores, supermarkets, and retail chains.
• Integrate with POS, inventory management, and ERP systems.
• Allow centralized monitoring of multiple locations.
summary: Innovation (4/5): draws on ai, computer vision applied to a smart automation problem, placing it in the breakthrough band. Feasibility (2/5): as a hardware build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (2/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Smart Automation. Tech Depth (4/5): centers on real-time, compliance. Sustainability (2/5): will need a maintenance/upkeep plan post-hackathon. Scalability (3/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 17/30 -> Yellow verdict.

detail.title: To build an AI-powered retail intelligence platform that delivers real-time shopper analytics, automated inventory visibility, and proactive queue management through on-device AI,enabling retailers to reduce stock-outs, improve customer experience, optimize staffing, and increase operational efficiency while maintaining privacy and minimizing cloud dependency.

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a smart-camera system for a store that watches shoppers, shelves, and checkout lines using AI running right on the camera device, so a store owner knows when a shelf's running empty or a queue's getting too long, without sending customer video to the cloud.
overview.why_it_matters: Small and mid-size Indian retailers lose money to stock-outs, slow checkouts, and poor staffing decisions, but most retail-analytics solutions assume reliable cloud connectivity, which Tier-2/3 city stores often don't have. On-device processing solves both the connectivity and privacy problems at once.
pain_points: Inventory shrinkage, stock-outs, and long queues are common but hard to detect and act on in real time without dedicated staff watching for them.
Many Indian retail stores, especially outside major cities, have limited or unreliable internet, ruling out cloud-dependent analytics.
Constant video streaming to the cloud is both a bandwidth cost and a real customer-privacy concern.
overview.background: India's retail sector spans millions of stores serving high daily customer volumes, facing challenges like inventory shrinkage, stock-outs, long billing queues, and limited visibility into shopper behavior, often under constrained internet connectivity. Recent edge-AI advances let cameras perform real-time analytics locally, improving privacy, reducing bandwidth, and enabling uninterrupted operation.
overview.whats_being_asked: An Intelligent Retail Analytics System using smart cameras and on-device AI to monitor shopper movement, inventory levels, and checkout queues in real time, without needing constant cloud processing, converting video into actionable business insights for staffing, restocking, and customer experience decisions.
expected_solution: Shopper analytics: traffic patterns, dwell time by store section.
Inventory visibility: detection of out-of-stock products and shelf-compliance monitoring.
Queue management: real-time congestion detection and prediction before it impacts customers.
All AI inference on-device/edge, preserving privacy and minimizing cloud/network dependency.
Business-facing dashboard converting raw detections into actionable insights.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Breakthrough band, but the innovation is really in the constraint (fully on-device, privacy-preserving, low-connectivity retail analytics), not the individual computer vision tasks, shopper tracking and shelf detection are well-known problems. Doing all three (shopper, shelf, queue) reliably on constrained edge hardware without a cloud fallback is the genuinely demanding part.
analysis.invention_effort_note: High. Three distinct computer vision tasks (people tracking/dwell-time, shelf/product detection, queue-length estimation) all running on-device is a lot of surface area, even before building the business-insights dashboard on top.

competitive_landscape.note: Retail analytics is a common commercial product category and a recognizable hackathon pitch, differentiation will come from actually demonstrating on-device inference (not a cloud API call dressed up as edge AI) and from picking a realistic subset of the three analytics types to build well.

innovation.note: Individually, shopper tracking, shelf detection, and queue estimation are known CV problems, the innovation is the fully-on-device, low-connectivity retail deployment constraint.

invention.note: Three separate detection tasks plus a unified business dashboard is meaningful breadth for 36 hours.

technical_feasibility.note: Building and validating all three analytics types (shopper, shelf, queue) reliably on real edge hardware is a stretch, pick one or two to fully demo and describe the third architecturally.

impact_and_benefits.note: Operational efficiency gains for retailers are real but less immediately dramatic to a judge than a safety or disaster-response use case, the pitch needs concrete numbers (e.g. reduced stock-out rate) to land well.

architecture.note: Each analytics module is fairly independent, they can be built and demoed in parallel without deep interdependency, which reduces integration risk relative to other PS in this batch.

overall_verdict.reasoning: A solid, achievable pick if the team fully builds 1-2 of the three analytics modules (shopper dwell-time and queue detection are the most visually demo-able) rather than spreading thin across all three, and frames the pitch around concrete operational metrics a retailer would actually care about.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: The three analytics categories are naturally modular, you can build and demo them somewhat independently, reducing the risk of one broken integration taking down the whole demo.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Trying to build shopper analytics, shelf compliance, and queue management all at full depth will likely leave all three shallow, pick your strongest 1-2 and go deep.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Confirm hour 0: do you have access to real or realistic retail-store camera footage (in-store CCTV-style video) for testing? If not, source or record proxy footage immediately, it's your core testing asset.

idea_0_4: Pick the 1-2 analytics modules to fully build (recommend: shopper dwell-time/traffic + queue-length detection, both are visually clear and don't need a curated product-shelf dataset).
Source or record test footage: either public retail-CCTV-style datasets or recorded proxy footage of people moving through a mock store/queue setup.
Assign owners: one per analytics module, one on the business-insights dashboard that ties detections together.
prototype_4_22: Build person-detection and tracking for shopper dwell-time/traffic patterns, using a lightweight on-device model (e.g. a compact YOLO variant).
Build queue-length estimation from the same or a second camera feed, counting people in a defined checkout zone over time.
In parallel, start the shelf/inventory module only if capacity allows, otherwise architect it and describe it as a planned extension.
integration_22_30: Wire detections into a unified dashboard: live traffic heatmap, dwell-time stats, current queue length with a simple congestion alert.
Verify the models actually run within a reasonable on-device compute budget, not just on a full laptop GPU, this is core to the PS's premise.
Test against your recorded/proxy footage across varied conditions (crowded vs sparse) to check robustness.
polish_30_36: Prepare a live or recorded demo showing the dashboard updating in real time as people move through frame.
Prepare concrete, retailer-facing framing: e.g. 'this would have flagged a 6-minute queue backup 4 minutes before it became a problem'.
Be honest about scope: clearly state which modules are fully built versus architecturally planned.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Frame every technical result in retailer-facing business terms (dwell time -> layout insight, queue length -> staffing trigger, stock-out detection -> restock alert) rather than raw CV metrics, judges evaluating a retail PS want to see the business translation, not just accuracy numbers.

strengths: Modular analytics categories reduce integration risk and allow a focused, deep build on 1-2 modules.
Clear, relatable real-world use case that's easy to explain to non-technical judges.
weaknesses: Less dramatic impact story than safety/disaster-focused PS in this batch, needs strong concrete framing to land.
Shelf/inventory detection specifically needs a labeled product dataset that may be hard to source quickly.

roles_needed: Someone to source/record realistic test footage
team_fit.ideal_ratio: 2 CV-focused to 1 backend, the detection accuracy is the credibility-defining part of the demo.
team_fit.approach: Record or source your test footage in the first hour, since every module depends on having realistic video to test against, don't let this become a bottleneck discovered at hour 10.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: Off-the-shelf person-detection/tracking model integration and dashboard UI scaffolding can be built quickly with AI coding assistance.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Tuning what counts as 'dwell time' versus just passing through, and what queue length triggers a real alert, needs human judgment calibrated against your specific test footage, not a generic default.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: An AI-generated pipeline claiming 'on-device inference' that was actually tested only on a laptop with a full GPU, never validated against a realistic edge-compute budget, misrepresents the PS's core premise, benchmark your actual inference speed on constrained hardware if you claim it.

data_resource_availability.status: Public pedestrian-tracking and queue-detection datasets exist and transfer reasonably well to a retail setting; curated retail-shelf/product-compliance datasets are thinner and harder to source quickly.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: If shelf/inventory detection data is too hard to source in time, drop that module from the live demo and present it as a planned extension using the same detection architecture.

judge_qna.question: Is this really running on-device, or is it a cloud API in disguise?
judge_qna.strong_answer: We benchmarked inference speed and resource usage on [specific edge hardware/constrained environment], here are the actual numbers, this isn't a cloud call, it's local inference.
judge_qna.follow_up: What's your frame rate and latency on that hardware, and how does accuracy trade off against it?

judge_qna.question: How do you protect shopper privacy if you're running cameras and tracking people?
judge_qna.strong_answer: We only extract aggregate movement statistics and never store identifiable video or facial data beyond the local inference frame, no raw video is retained or transmitted.
judge_qna.follow_up: Walk us through exactly what data, if any, persists after a shopper leaves the frame.

judge_qna.question: How would a small store owner with no technical staff actually deploy and use this?
judge_qna.strong_answer: The dashboard is designed for a non-technical retailer, plain-language alerts (e.g. 'Aisle 3 queue building up') rather than raw analytics, and setup is a single camera pointed at the area of interest.
judge_qna.follow_up: What's the actual hardware cost and setup time you're estimating for a small retailer?
